name: 911 SSPO Award Review
description: Runs off an award package (folder of order folders) and estimates plate cutting time from ACTUAL D911 throughput: a pieces-per-hour table by thickness band derived from 18.5 months of closed actuals (includes setup/handling), plus stock/material/thickness from each nest's work-package PDF. The old exact-linear-inch times (each work order's DXF geometry / a thickness-driven feed rate) are still computed as reference columns at the far right. Writes ONE consolidated Excel workbook - Plates and Non-Plates sheets, every batch-list column plus generated columns (Division placeholder, linear inches, Pcs/Hr, Est Min/PC, Est Min/WO, Est Cut Hours, then the LI reference block and the packet's EB Machine / EB Fuel) - each followed by a real, refreshable PivotTable (one line per nest: Parts + Cut Time in both hours and minutes), plus a Shape Ft Req sheet totalling each shape nest's stock feet from its Summary of Batches lengths (rounded up to the foot per length) for receiving, and a Working Forecast Input sheet (one line per nest: Source Material / Pieces / Orders from the nest packet, shape Total Ft Req, blank REM Used / REM Made / Operations) that copy-pastes straight into the Working Forecast List. Prompts for the ROOT directory at runtime.
author: Anthony Sieben

setup: Have the award package folder ready - the ROOT whose subfolders are the order folders (this runs pre-batch).
Each order needs its NEST PACKAGES packet PDFs and batch list; the plate cut-time reference columns also use the IGES DXFs.
You pick the ROOT when it runs; wrapper / extraction folders around the orders are handled automatically.
how_it_works: Pick the award ROOT. The app reads stock, material, and thickness from the packet PDFs and batch list.
It estimates plate cut time from actual shop throughput (pieces per hour by thickness), keeps the exact linear-inch times as reference columns, and rolls it all up in a pivot.
It also builds a Shape Ft Req sheet for receiving and a Working Forecast Input sheet ready to paste into the forecast.
output: One workbook with Plates and Non-Plates sheets, a real Excel pivot of cut hours per nest, a Shape Ft Req sheet, and a Working Forecast Input sheet.

fields.label: Output Directory (optional)
fields.description: Where to save the consolidated estimate workbook. Leave blank to save inside the ROOT directory you pick at runtime.
